Check a value in place

Source: R/claim.R
claim.Rd

claim(x, <check>, ...) returns x visibly and unchanged, so a value can be guarded inside a larger expression: trend(claim(foo, . > 0)) (rule 3.1.1). In a check, . stands for x (rule 3.1.2); other names are looked up in the caller. Each check is a separate argument and is reported separately (rule 3.1.3). Checks are captured unevaluated, and a failure quotes the check as written (rule 3.1.4).

Usage

claim(x, ..., level = c("fail", "warn"))

Arguments

x

Any value.

...

One or more checks, as expressions in . and the caller's variables.

level

"fail" (the default) or "warn". It must be given by name.

Value

x, unchanged.

Details

A check passes only when it evaluates to a single TRUE.

Outside a knit a failed check stops with an error of class weft_claim_failed. claim(x) with no check stops with class weft_claim_no_check (rule 3.1.10).

With level = "warn" a check that is not TRUE is a warning, not a failure. In a knit the value prints as if the check had passed, no marker is left and the render does not fail; the check is recorded in last_knit()$warnings, and the warnings are printed to stderr at the end of the knit. Outside a knit it is a warning() of class weft_claim_warning, and x is returned. A check that itself raises an error is a failed check at the level given.

Examples

claim(5, . > 1)
#> [1] 5
claim(c(3, 4), sum(.) == 7, all(. > 0))
#> [1] 3 4
